name: Silver Key Apartments at North Weber
headline: Silver Key Apartments at North Weber is a 49-unit, all-affordable new-construction building for older adults (62+) at 30% to 60% AMI on a vacant lot at 2126 N. Weber Street in Colorado Springs' Old North End, sponsored by nonprofit Silver Key Senior Services, which won a 2026 Round One federal 9% and state housing tax credit award.
why_it_matters: It shows a nonprofit service provider pairing a 9% deal with deeply discounted land ($350,000 against a $1.31M appraisal), city HOME money, county debt and a turnkey developer (MGL Partners), and getting a 49-unit building approved on an office-residential lot through a conditional use and a development standards adjustment, with affordable housing counted as the compensating benefit.

status.label: Credits awarded and land-use approvals granted; construction start not confirmed
status.detail: City Planning Commission approved the conditional use and development standards adjustment on 2026-01-14. An administrative development plan was still required. CHFA announced the award on 2026-05-21. In July 2026 KOAA reported that construction is "set to begin in February" (year not stated; 2027 is inferred). There is no public record of a building permit, financial closing or groundbreaking.

next_step: Watch for the City's administrative Development Plan decision for 2126 N. Weber Street, a City Council or county action on the $600,000 HOME and $500,000 El Paso County loans, and a building permit ahead of the reported February start.

key_numbers.meaning: 47 one-bedrooms and 2 two-bedrooms: 5 units at 30% AMI, 21 at 50% and 23 at 60% (average 52.65% AMI).
About $16.97M over the 10-year credit period (calculated), plus $500,000 in standard state credit. The application priced the federal credit at $0.81 for $13,749,675 of equity.
From the February 2026 application narrative; below the roughly $497,900 Colorado per-unit average the narrative cites.
The seller sold at a deep discount in September 2025 but can buy the land back at 110% of the price if construction of low-income senior housing has not started by 2028-09-05.

background.text: The site was a State Division of Wildlife office from the 1960s; the state left in 2005 and the buildings were removed around 2011. A 2017 City approval for a 44-unit apartment building was never built and expired in 2023, and the empty lot drew complaints about camping, weeds and trash.

Silver Key bought the land in September 2025 for $350,000 against a July 2025 appraisal of $1,310,000 and owns it free and clear. The purchase agreement lets the seller repurchase at 110% of the price if construction of low-income senior housing has not begun within 36 months of closing (by 2028-09-05). The seller is not named.

On 2026-01-14 the City Planning Commission approved a conditional use for multifamily in the OR zone (CUDP-25-0030) and a development standards adjustment to allow 49 units in one building where 10 is the maximum (DVSA-25-0009). Affordable housing was the compensating benefit. The vote was reported as unanimous.

City staff said a Development Plan is still required; it is decided administratively but with public notice. Engineering flagged possible paving of the west alley, and on-street parking on narrow Madison Street (26 feet wide) is to be reviewed at that stage.
The staff report says affordability will be fixed by a future deed restriction or land use restriction agreement. The length of the affordability period is not stated in the public sources checked.
Public comment was mixed: 15 emails plus calls and a neighborhood meeting, with concerns about building size, parking and alley traffic, and support for replacing a nuisance lot with senior housing.
This is Silver Key's second LIHTC development after the 50-unit Silver Key Apartments at South Murray, also delivered with MGL; Silver Key reported a waitlist of over 410 applicants.
Silver Key set a goal of raising $800,000 for a legacy fund to help offset rents for residents at or below 30% AMI.

CHFA's Round One letter-of-intent list (2025-12-08) showed the deal at 49 units seeking $1,700,000 in federal and $500,000 in state credit; the February 2026 application requested $1,697,491, the amount awarded.

discrepancies.text: Unit count: KOAA's November 2025 report described 47 units and the Gazette's December 2025 site-plan article described 50 units (47 one-bedroom and 3 two-bedroom), while the City staff report, the CHFA application and the award report give 49 units (47 one-bedroom and 2 two-bedroom).
Site size: the City staff report and staff presentation give 1.31 acres (57,064 sq ft), while the CHFA application narrative and KOAA give about 1.22 acres (1.223 acres).

Construction start: the Gazette in January 2026 said construction could start that summer, the Gazette in May 2026 said groundbreaking was expected later in 2026, the application narrative said the project would be ready to start by April 2027, and KOAA in July 2026 said construction was set to begin in February.

open_questions: Has the administrative Development Plan been approved, and has a building permit been issued?
Have the $600,000 City HOME funds and the $500,000 El Paso County loan been formally approved, or was the HOME money replaced with local funds to avoid Build America, Buy America costs?
The narrative's listed sources add to $20,207,532, about $1.6M less than its stated $21,807,532 total cost (calculated); the source of the difference is not public.
The narrative shows $500,000 of state credit equity at $0.70 against a $500,000 state credit award; how the state credit is counted is not explained publicly.
Lender, equity investor, final rents, affordability period and the land seller's identity are not public.
